name: dispatches_registered_agent
why: v3.16.0 dispatch-shape rebuild WP0/WP3: the wrapper dispatches the registered agent, not a hand-rolled general-purpose prompt — same contract as dispatching-task-loop's own pairing with shipyard-disciplined-builder.

name: no_general_purpose
why: check_dispatch_contract_pairs also enforces this structurally; pinned here too as a content-level regression guard, matching dispatching-task-loop.json's own convention.

name: coordinator_never_builds_never_certifies
why: the agent's own role section states its three-word job description — dispatcher, not builder, not verifier.

name: coordinator_never_commits_or_writes
why: §4.2 property 1/2 — no Write/Edit/Bash tool, so there is no uncommitted work to lose and no way to forge a task-return.

name: coordinator_tools_allowlist_exact
why: the exact frontmatter allowlist is what makes 'cannot certify, cannot commit' structural — no Bash means it cannot invoke shipyard-data at all.

name: coordinator_has_status_complete_return
why: Required Return Shape covers all three coordinator outcomes.

name: coordinator_has_status_partial_return
why: a track where some tasks completed and others blocked is a distinct, named outcome from full COMPLETE or full BLOCKED.

name: coordinator_has_status_blocked_return
why: covers missing-brief-parameters and structural dispatch-failure cases.

name: coordinator_has_track_notes_field
why: §4.2 property 4 — the running TRACK NOTES block is the concrete artifact that makes the coordinator's persistence load-bearing rather than an extra agent buying nothing.

name: coordinator_sequential_dispatch
why: dispatch within a track is one builder at a time, never two in flight under the same coordinator — bounds the nested concurrency budget.

name: coordinator_deterministic_builder_naming
why: §4.7 — deterministic naming is what lets main TaskStop a specific nested builder by name later, since TaskStop is ownership-scoped and the coordinator cannot stop its own children.

name: coordinator_isolation_worktree_on_builders
why: every nested builder dispatch passes isolation: "worktree", preserving one-task-one-worktree-one-branch.

name: coordinator_interface_change_broadcast
why: a completed builder revealing a shared interface change is broadcast to sibling track coordinators by name — the concrete use of sibling_track_names.

name: coordinator_blocked_does_not_halt_track
pattern: does not stop your track|do not halt the whole track
why: rule 5 — a block on one task must not stop the rest of an independently-buildable track.

name: coordinator_sendmessage_toolsearch_first
why: SendMessage is deferred in an isolated context and fails silently without a ToolSearch promotion first — the coordinator's only reporting channel, so this must be its first action.

name: wrapper_orchestrator_side_parsing_and_gating
why: v3.16.0: relocated from ship-execute.json's team_lead_runs_orchestrator_gate — this section now lives in the wrapper skill (dispatching-track-coordinator owns the dispatch mechanics, per the v3.12.0 agent-extraction sort rule), not in ship-execute/references/track-mode.md, so the pin moved with it.

name: wrapper_reuses_per_task_gate
why: the per-task orchestrator-side gate (sha verify + PROBE_EXIT:0 + anti-stub-scan) is unchanged from dispatching-task-loop, applied per task inside a track exactly as outside one.

name: wrapper_single_redispatch_rule_reused
why: a BLOCKED task inside a track is redispatched directly via dispatching-task-loop's own single-redispatch rule, not re-run through a fresh coordinator.

name: wrapper_silent_return_track_level
why: v3.12.0 anti-silence contract: a coordinator return with no STATUS: line is its own named, audited outcome — reconcile against .subagent-returns/ before assuming anything is lost, redispatch once, then park.

name: wrapper_silent_return_reconciles_ground_truth
pattern: Reconcile against ground truth before assuming anything is lost
why: nested builders write .subagent-returns/<task_id>.json independent of the coordinator, so a silent coordinator does not by itself mean lost work — the wrapper must check the shared data dir before redispatching.

name: wrapper_never_trusts_coordinator_claim_alone
why: a COMPLETED_TASKS/BLOCKED_TASKS csv that doesn't account for every task in the track's input is treated as untrustworthy, same discipline as the per-task gate — the coordinator cannot self-certify a track any more than a builder can self-certify a task.

name: render_before_ask_rule
why: check_render_before_ask scans every skill with an AskUserQuestion mention, capability skills included since v3.11.0's zero-exemption widening.

name: render_provenance_negation
why: anchors the same phrase check_render_before_ask requires — a coordinator's BLOCKED reason or a redispatch's REASON must be rendered as chat text, not just present in a subagent return, before the ask.

name: render_before_ask_compact_card
why: third leg of the render-before-ask contract — question/option strings display as a compact card, not a rendering surface.

name: no_taskcreate_taskupdate_in_wrapper_flow
pattern: the coordinator calls TaskCreate|the coordinator calls TaskUpdate|coordinator.{0,20}TaskList\(\)
why: C1 — isolated agents (the coordinator included) have no Task* access at all; the wrapper must never describe the coordinator itself touching the checklist. Main is the sole Task* owner.
